cards.method: Kaplan-Meier and Nelson-Aalen estimators with the log-rank family of tests
cards.when: estimating a survival or cumulative-hazard curve from right-censored durations, and comparing curves across groups without assuming a parametric shape
cards.when_not: you need covariates (-> #Cox); the durations are interval-censored; the outcome is competing risks (-> cumulative incidence); you want a parametric time-to-event distribution

alternatives.criterion: you need to adjust for covariates rather than compare raw curves
more than one mutually exclusive failure type
you want a smooth closed-form survival function and extrapolation

output_key_fields: survival/cumhazard: the step function on the observed event times
lower/upper: pointwise confidence band at conf_level
median_survival: the first time the curve crosses 0.5, None if it never does
logrank: statistic, df and p_value for equality of curves across groups
interpretation_traps: the curve is only identified up to the largest observed time; beyond it the estimate is undefined, not flat
median_survival is None when the curve never reaches 0.5 -- that is heavy censoring, not an error
the log-rank test assumes proportional hazards; with crossing curves it loses power and can be near-zero for a real difference

cards.method: Cox proportional-hazards regression with time-varying covariates and stratification
cards.when: estimating covariate effects on the hazard of an event without committing to a baseline hazard shape; hazard ratios are the quantity of interest
cards.when_not: the proportional-hazards assumption fails and cannot be repaired by stratification (-> AFT); you want an absolute survival prediction rather than a ratio; there are competing risks

alternatives.criterion: you need a closed-form survival function or to extrapolate beyond the data
the hazards are non-proportional in a small number of discrete strata
durations are recorded in coarse intervals with many ties

output_key_fields: params/coef: log hazard ratios; exp(coef) is the hazard ratio
bse, z, p_value, conf_int: Wald inference on the log scale
baseline_cumhazard: the Breslow estimate of the baseline
loglike, concordance: fit and discrimination
interpretation_traps: coefficients are on the LOG hazard scale -- exponentiate before reading them as hazard ratios
a hazard ratio is not a risk ratio and does not integrate to one over time
ties are handled by an approximation; with heavy tying the Efron and Breslow handlers disagree materially
stratification removes the strata's main effect from the estimate entirely -- it is not a control variable

cards.method: Parametric accelerated-failure-time models: Weibull, log-normal, log-logistic and exponential
cards.when: you want a smooth closed-form survival function, the ability to extrapolate beyond the last observed time, or a time-ratio interpretation rather than a hazard ratio
cards.when_not: you are unwilling to commit to a distributional shape (-> Cox); the shape is clearly non-monotonic in a way none of the four families capture

alternatives.criterion: you do not want to assume a baseline shape
the hazard shape is complex and the four families all fit badly
no covariates and no extrapolation needed

output_key_fields: params: coefficients on the LOG time scale; exp(coef) is a time ratio
scale/shape: the fitted distribution parameters
aic, bic, loglike: for choosing among the four families
predicted_median/predicted_mean: fitted survival summaries
interpretation_traps: an AFT coefficient is a TIME ratio, not a hazard ratio -- a positive coefficient lengthens survival
only the Weibull and exponential are simultaneously AFT and proportional-hazards; for the others the two scales disagree
the exponential imposes a constant hazard, which is almost never right for economic durations and shows up as a poor AIC rather than an error
extrapolation beyond the data is the point of the model and also its main risk
sources: Kalbfleisch & Prentice 2002, The Statistical Analysis of Failure Time Data, 2nd ed.

cards.method: Discrete-time hazard models with complementary log-log and logit links
cards.when: durations are recorded in coarse intervals -- months, quarters, waves -- so ties are pervasive and a continuous-time model is a fiction
cards.when_not: durations are measured finely enough for a continuous-time model (-> Cox/AFT); there is no person-period expansion available

alternatives.alt: Cox with an appropriate tie handler
alternatives.criterion: the discreteness is mild and the grid is fine
you want a closed-form continuous survival function
the exit is to more than one competing destination

output_key_fields: params: coefficients on the link scale; cloglog recovers the proportional-hazards parameter
baseline_hazard: the fitted hazard at each duration interval
survival: the implied discrete survivor function
loglike, aic: fit
interpretation_traps: the input must be a PERSON-PERIOD table -- one row per unit per interval at risk -- not one row per unit
with a cloglog link the coefficients are the underlying continuous-time proportional-hazards parameters; with a logit link they are not
the baseline must be modelled explicitly (dummies, polynomial or spline in duration); omitting it forces a flat hazard
unobserved heterogeneity biases duration dependence toward negative -- the estimated hazard falls even when the true one does not
sources: Jenkins 2005, Survival Analysis (unpublished manuscript, University of Essex)

cards.method: Competing risks: cause-specific hazards, cumulative incidence and the Fine-Gray subdistribution model
cards.when: a unit can exit to more than one mutually exclusive destination and treating the other destinations as censoring would overstate the risk of the one you care about
cards.when_not: there is only one failure type (-> Kaplan-Meier/Cox); the destinations are not mutually exclusive

alternatives.criterion: you want the effect on the hazard of one cause among those still at risk
you want the effect on the observable cumulative incidence
wrong here -- it treats competing events as censoring and overstates incidence

output_key_fields: cumulative_incidence: the CIF per cause, which sums with the survivor function to one
cause_specific: per-cause hazard-model coefficients
subdistribution: Fine-Gray coefficients, on the CIF scale
gray_test: statistic and p_value for equality of CIFs across groups
interpretation_traps: ONE minus Kaplan-Meier is NOT the cumulative incidence under competing risks -- it is biased upward, sometimes severely
a cause-specific hazard ratio and a subdistribution hazard ratio answer different questions and routinely point in opposite directions
the CIFs of all causes plus the survivor function must sum to one; a set that does not is a sign the events were not mutually exclusive

cards.method: Frailty and shared-frailty models for unobserved heterogeneity
cards.when: units are clustered, or duration dependence is suspected to be contaminated by unobserved heterogeneity, and you want to separate the two
cards.when_not: there is no clustering and no reason to expect heterogeneity; the sample is too small to identify a frailty variance

alternatives.criterion: you only need correct inference, not a heterogeneity estimate
the clusters are few and you can afford a baseline per cluster
durations are interval-recorded

output_key_fields: params: covariate effects conditional on the frailty
frailty_variance: theta, the dispersion of the unobserved term; zero means no heterogeneity
loglike, aic: fit
lrt_frailty: likelihood-ratio test of theta = 0, which is on the boundary
interpretation_traps: the test of theta = 0 sits on the boundary of the parameter space, so the null distribution is a mixture and the naive p-value is conservative
conditional (frailty) and marginal (population-average) coefficients differ; they are not interchangeable
unobserved heterogeneity and genuine negative duration dependence are only weakly separated -- identification comes from the functional form, not from the data
sources: Hougaard 2000, Analysis of Multivariate Survival Data
Lancaster 1990, The Econometric Analysis of Transition Data

cards.method: Proportional-hazards diagnostics: Schoenfeld residuals and time-interaction tests
cards.when: checking the assumption a Cox model rests on, before its hazard ratios are reported as if they held at every horizon
cards.when_not: the model is not a proportional-hazards model (an AFT needs different diagnostics); the sample has too few events for residual patterns to be readable

alternatives.criterion: the violation is confined to a discrete variable you do not need an estimate for
the violation is a smooth trend in the log hazard ratio
the violation is pervasive across covariates

output_key_fields: schoenfeld: scaled residuals per covariate per event time
zph: per-covariate and global test of a zero slope against time
slope: the fitted trend, which is the direction the hazard ratio drifts
martingale/deviance: residuals for functional-form and outlier checks
interpretation_traps: the global test is not a substitute for the per-covariate tests -- a large violation in one direction can cancel another
the test depends on the time transform: identity, log and rank transforms disagree, and a violation visible under one can vanish under another
a significant test with a very large sample can flag a violation too small to matter; read the slope, not just the p-value
martingale residuals are strongly skewed by construction and must not be read as approximately normal

cards.method: Spell duration dependence and hazard-shape estimation
cards.when: the question is the SHAPE of the hazard over the spell -- whether exit rates rise or fall with elapsed duration, as in unemployment or firm-survival studies
cards.when_not: you only need covariate effects (-> Cox); the spells are too short or too few for a shape to be identified

alternatives.criterion: you want a readable shape with no functional-form commitment
a monotone shape is enough and you want one parameter for it
you must separate true duration dependence from unobserved heterogeneity

output_key_fields: hazard: the estimated hazard on the duration grid
shape: increasing / decreasing / non-monotonic, with the turning point where one exists
weibull_p: the Weibull shape parameter, where p > 1 is positive duration dependence
conf_band: pointwise band on the hazard
interpretation_traps: unobserved heterogeneity biases the estimated hazard DOWNWARD over the spell -- apparent negative duration dependence is the single most common artefact in this literature
the piecewise grid drives the answer: too few intervals hide the shape, too many make it noise
the hazard near the largest observed duration rests on very few units still at risk and its band is correspondingly wide
sources: Van den Berg 2001, Duration models: specification, identification and multiple durations (Handbook of Econometrics 5)
